title: New Support Will Help Strengthen Indonesia’s Tax System, Improve Development Spending

locator: Press release lead and paragraphs describing the two reform pillars
source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with specific financing and reform details; strong temporal fit to 2022 policy execution.
period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to Jokowi’s 2019-2024 administration.
ruler_attribution: Government-level fiscal reform under Jokowi’s administration; not a personal act by Jokowi alone, but within executive policy control.
contrary_evidence: World Bank notes Indonesia’s tax revenues were still low versus peers.

title: New Financing Will Support Indonesia to Improve and Protect Human Capital
claim: The World Bank approved a $350 million loan to support Indonesia’s human capital agenda by safeguarding income protection, increasing access to healthcare services, preventing unhealthy behavior, and improving the effectiveness of government spending; it also said Indonesia’s Human Capital Index improved from 0.50 to 0.54 between 2010 and 2020 but remained below peers.
locator: Press release lead and human capital paragraphs
source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with clear policy content, funding amount, and time fit.
period_fit: 2022 policy support and retrospective human-capital comparison relevant to the Jokowi period.
ruler_attribution: Government-level reform agenda; attribution to Jokowi is indirect but real through executive control of social and fiscal policy.
contrary_evidence: World Bank says education, social insurance, and stunting remained weak relative to peers.

title: Cash Direct Assistance Distribution for Fuel Oil Subsidy Reallocation Reaches up to 95.9 Percent
claim: President Jokowi said BLT BBM distribution had reached 19.7 million beneficiaries, or 95.9 percent of the target, after the government reallocated fuel subsidies to maintain purchasing power.
locator: Paragraph quoting the President after observing distribution in Baubau
source_confidence_reason: Official presidential statement with a specific implementation metric and date.
period_fit: Direct 2022 implementation evidence within the target period.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi’s announced policy shift and oversight of rollout, though execution was carried out by ministries and post offices.
contrary_evidence: The measure is short-term relief; it does not prove long-run efficiency or equitable targeting by itself.

title: Economic Minister: State Budget Deficit Smaller than Target
claim: The 2022 State Budget deficit was 2.38 percent of GDP, smaller than the target stated in law, and fiscal consolidation was achieved faster than planned.
locator: Quoted statement by Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto after the cabinet meeting led by President Jokowi
source_confidence_reason: Official government summary of a fiscal year outcome with a precise deficit figure and date.
period_fit: Retrospective on fiscal year 2022; directly relevant to Jokowi’s 2022 economic management.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Jokowi administration’s fiscal policy and cabinet coordination; not solely to Jokowi personally.
contrary_evidence: Deficit performance partly benefited from stronger revenue conditions and cyclical recovery.

title: BPK Gives Unqualified Opinion on 2022 Financial Statements of Central Government
claim: BPK gave an unqualified opinion on the central government’s 2022 financial statements; 81 of 82 line ministries and the state treasury statements also received unqualified opinions, and BPK said most fiscal-transparency criteria were met, while noting audit findings totaling Rp25.85 trillion.
locator: Press release body and transparency paragraph
source_confidence_reason: Primary audit-board release on FY2022 accounts with concrete audit outcomes and transparency language.
period_fit: Retrospective FY2022 evidence; directly relevant to Jokowi’s administrative and fiscal management record.
ruler_attribution: Government-wide financial management under Jokowi’s cabinet; the audit is not personal proof but is strong evidence of implementation quality.
contrary_evidence: BPK also reported material findings and internal-control weaknesses, so the result is positive but not clean.

title: As children in Indonesia return to school, UNICEF calls for urgent action to address learning crisis
claim: UNICEF said extended school closures and disrupted reopenings affected around 60 million students in Indonesia and caused significant learning loss, with harms especially acute for vulnerable students.
locator: First and second paragraphs of the press release
source_confidence_reason: UNICEF is a strong independent source on education disruptions, and the claim is specific and contemporaneous.
period_fit: Directly within 2022, though the shock is partly inherited from the pandemic rather than uniquely Jokowi’s creation.
ruler_attribution: Attribution to Jokowi is limited; this is mainly a constraint and implementation challenge for the administration’s recovery response rather than a ruler-caused collapse.
contrary_evidence: The article primarily reflects pandemic inheritance; it does not isolate Jokowi’s personal policy failure.

title: Indonesia Poverty Assessment: Pathway Towards Economic Security
claim: The World Bank said Indonesia had made remarkable poverty-reduction progress and extreme poverty was basically eradicated by 2022, but more than one-third of Indonesians remained economically insecure and could be pushed into poverty by shocks; it urged broader opportunity creation, protection, and resilience investments.
source_confidence_reason: Independent World Bank assessment with explicit 2022 retrospective and policy interpretation.
period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 conditions and policy trajectory.
ruler_attribution: Broadly attributable to the Jokowi period, but the result reflects long-run reform, commodity conditions, and recovery as well as current administration choices.
contrary_evidence: The assessment says economic insecurity remained high, so the progress is real but incomplete.

title: Presiden Jokowi Sampaikan Progres Pembangunan IKN
claim: Jokowi said the government had started infrastructure work in the core Nusantara capital area, that the raw-water dam would be completed in January, and that ministry, presidential, and vice-presidential buildings would begin construction in December.
locator: Lead paragraph and presidential quotes in the news item
source_confidence_reason: Official presidential update with direct statements on 2022 implementation milestones.
period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to a flagship Jokowi program.
ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Jokowi as a personal flagship policy and executive priority, although much implementation was delegated to ministries and the IKN authority.
contrary_evidence: This is initiation evidence, not completion; success depended on later delivery and financing.

title: Indonesia Targets Low Vaccination Areas to Tackle Decline in Childhood Immunization
claim: WHO said Indonesia achieved 94.6 percent full immunization coverage in 2022, exceeding the national target of 94.1 percent, and that the BIAN catch-up campaign reached 26.5 million children with measles-rubella vaccines, 1.3 million with polio vaccines, and 2 million with DTP-HB-Hib vaccines.
source_confidence_reason: WHO retrospective on 2022 national immunization performance with precise coverage and campaign figures.
period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 campaign and coverage; acceptable as target-period evidence.
ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Jokowi’s administration through Ministry of Health coordination, though the campaign was operationally carried by health officials and local governments.
contrary_evidence: WHO also noted outbreaks in low-vaccination areas, so the win was uneven and not fully durable.
